Håll dig till tillåtna vägar; klättra inte på murar eller kasta ting i skållhål/vallgrav. Nattbesök endast om officiellt arrangerat; ingen otillåten spökjakt. Respektera personal och fotoregler.

places.name: Kalmar Slott
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Kalmar Slott on Kalmarsund is one of Sweden's greatest historical mystery destinations — roughly 800 years of layered fortress and palace history, long called "Rikets nyckel" (the Key to the Kingdom) for its place on the old Danish border. A defensive tower rose here around 1180; Magnus Ladulås built a ring-wall fortress in the late 1200s; in 1397 the Kalmar Union was forged in this political landscape. Under Gustav Vasa, Erik XIV and Johan III the medieval stronghold became one of Northern Europe's finest Renaissance castles — still largely legible as in 1592. After Roskilde (1658) it lost its border role and served as prison and crown distillery. Court records from 1645 document the terror of inmate Ölands-Jödde, who dominated the communal prison and murdered fellow prisoners before being hanged. Folklore adds the White Lady (often linked to Anna Bielke), Grey Lady, and a mysterious child, while the castle itself runs seasonal ghost walks mixing myth with dark history. Haunted Sweden keeps SFV/museum facts separate from legend. Visit year-round exhibitions; book official autumn ghost walks for after-dark atmosphere.
places.whyItFitsHauntedSweden: Flagship Renaissance fortress: 800+ years of documented history, Kalmar Union and Vasa dynasty, Key to the Kingdom strategic mythos, preserved prison narrative including Ölands-Jödde, official ghost walks (Svarta Damen / Tystad och begravd and related programmes), outstanding towers and moat photography. Visual 10/10, historical value 10/10, royal history 10/10, folklore strength 9.5/10, paranormal reputation 9.5/10 — Haunted Sweden Score 9.8. Premium content potential EXTREMELY HIGH; research confidence HIGH. Ideal verification mission: full photography, official ghost walk, prison documentation, guide interviews, folklore vs court records, documentary episode (pair with Gråborg / Borgholm / Blå Jungfrun for a Kalmar Strait route).
places.shortDescription: Renaissance "Key to the Kingdom" on Kalmarsund — Vasa palace, Kalmar Union landmark, castle prison, and official ghost walks.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Kalmar Slott stands at Kungsgatan 1, Kalmar (Småland), on Kalmarsund. Owned/managed in the state heritage system (SFV property; museum and events via Kalmar Slott). ORIGINS: Around 1180 a kastal (defensive tower) was built against pirates and enemies; Kalmar was an established town by the early 1200s. In the late 1200s Magnus Ladulås developed a ring-wall fortress with towers around the old kastal (Kuretornet marks the old western main entrance) — then among Sweden's most modern fortifications. STRATEGIC ROLE: For centuries the castle guarded Sweden's southern approaches while Skåne, Blekinge and Halland remained Danish (until 1658); it was called Rikets nyckel — "the Key to the Kingdom." KALMAR UNION: In 1397 Queen Margaret engineered the union of Sweden, Norway and Denmark; negotiations are tied to Kalmar, and Erik of Pomerania was crowned union king in Kalmar's town church. The union ended formally with Gustav Vasa's kingship in 1523. VASA RENAISSANCE: Mid–late 1500s Gustav I, Erik XIV and Johan III transformed the medieval fortress into a continental-style Renaissance palace (corner towers from the 1530s onward; European artists and craftsmen under Erik and Johan). Interiors include the King's chamber with early intarsia view of the castle and a secret passage, and the Golden Hall's unique gilded coffered ceiling. Appearance remains close to the late-16th-century fabric (often summarised as "as in 1592"). WAR: In the Kalmar War, commandant Christer Somme surrendered the castle to the Danes on 3 August 1611 after hard fighting; Danish occupation until 1613. After the Peace of Roskilde (1658) Kalmar ceased to be a Danish-border fortress; royal visits dwindled and halls were reused as prison and crown distillery (kronobränneri). PRISON — ÖLANDS-JÖDDE (documented court history, not paranormal): December 1645 Kalmar town court (rådhusrätt) tried the inmate known as Ölands-Jödde. Roughly 36 prisoners shared a communal cell; Jödde and associates ran a terror regime — a mock "court," extortion of weekly food/fuel money for beer, beatings, and killings of fellow inmates (popular and historical summaries cite multiple murders by beating plus deaths from starvation/neglect; warders and officials were implicated in corruption). Jödde was sentenced to death by hanging. Treat Hofrén and later retellings as based on the court case, not ghost evidence. RESTORATION: 19th-century decay nearly stripped interiors; Fredrik Wilhelm Scholander and pupil Helgo Zettervall led restoration completed about 1891; moat restored 1941; later 20th–21st-century conservation. Today: museum, exhibitions, restaurant, guided tours and seasonal events. DARK HISTORY CONTEXT: Border warfare, sieges, political imprisonment, torture/interrogation traditions in fortress prisons, executions, disease and hunger among inmates — heavy emotional legacy of a working fortress-prison, separate from folklore below.
places.legend: FOLKLORE — WHITE LADY / VITA FRUN (not proven as a named haunting): Local tradition describes a woman with a lantern seen in towers or windows; Destination Kalmar storytelling often identifies her with early-16th-century noblewoman Anna Bielke, who defended Kalmar interests against Danish pressure — present the lantern defender tale as folklore layered on a historical figure. FOLKLORE — GREY LADY / GRÅA DAMEN: Another female apparition tradition in popular ghost lists. FOLKLORE — LITTLE BOY: Modern visitor/guide anecdotes of a mysterious child inside the castle — unverified. FOLKLORE — PRISON SPIRITS: Stories linking residual unrest to former inmates (including Jödde's era) — keep court facts in HISTORY and ghost claims here. OFFICIAL GHOST WALLS (cultural programming): Kalmar Slott runs autumn ghost walks through darkened halls and prison areas (e.g. programmes led by "Svarta Damen"; titles such as Tystad och begravd / Ur mörkrets skuggor), explicitly mixing myths with real dark history; age limits typically apply. WITNESS REPORTS (anecdotal): Footsteps; whispering voices; shadow figures; doors opening; cold spots; apparitions; guide and visitor experiences in prison vaults and empty rooms. SPECIAL AREAS: castle prison (strongest historical atmosphere; Ölands-Jödde); royal apartments; vaults and cellars; courtyard (night photography when access allows); castle chapel. ATMOSPHERE: Massive Renaissance towers, stone courts, moat reflections, hidden stairs — one of Sweden's most atmospheric castles after dark. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: official ghost walk; prison history vs folklore; EVP only where permitted; moat blue-hour photography; Grey/White Lady archive check. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, blue hour. Keep DOCUMENTED castle/court history separate from FOLKLORE and walk entertainment above.
places.safetyNote: Active museum and event site — visit during official hours via kalmarslott.se. Guided tours included with admission when offered; seasonal ghost walks require separate tickets and age rules. Stay on allowed routes; do not enter closed towers, prison sections or scaffolding without guides. Respect moat edges, fire rules and photography policy. No unauthorized overnight investigation inside the castle.

Gustav Vasa, Erik XIV och Johan III skapar renässanspalats (nära 1592-skick). Kalmarkriget: kapitulation 3 augusti 1611, danskt till 1613. Efter Roskilde 1658: fängelse och kronobränneri. ÖLANDS-JÖDDE (rådhusrätt december 1645): terrorvälde bland ca 36 gemensamhetsfångar, misshandel och mord på medfångar, hängning — dokumenterad brottshistoria, inte spökbevis. Restaurering Scholander/Zettervall ca 1891; vallgrav 1941. Idag museum, restaurang, visningar. Mörk historia som kontext: krig, fångenskap, avrättningar, sjukdom — håll isär från folklore.

OFFICIELLA SPÖKVANDRINGAR: t.ex. Svarta Damen / Tystad och begravd — blandar myt och mörk historia. VITTNESMÅL: fotsteg, viskningar, skuggor, dörrar, köld. OMRÅDEN: fängelse, kungavåningar, valv, borggård, slottskyrka.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Kalmar slott vid Kalmarsund är ett av Sveriges starkaste historiska mysteriemål — ca 800 år från kastal till Vasarenässans, länge kallat Rikets nyckel. Här knöts Kalmarunionen 1397; efter 1658 blev salarna fängelse. Domstolshandlingar 1645 dokumenterar Ölands-Jöddes terror bland medfångar. Folklore om Vita frun och Gråa damen samt slottets egna spökvandringar hålls isär från SFV:s och museets fakta. Besök utställningar året runt; boka officiella höstvandringar för mörkrets atmosfär.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt museum och evenemang – besök under officiella tider via kalmarslott.se. Guidningar enligt entré; säsongens spökvandringar kräver egen biljett och åldersregler. Håll dig till tillåtna vägar; gå inte in i stängda torn eller fängelseytor utan guide. Respektera vallgrav, brandskydd och fotoregler. Ingen otillåten nattutredning inne i slottet.

places.name: Furunäset
places.englishName: Furunäset (Former Furunäsets Sjukhus / Piteå Hospital och Asyl)
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Furunäset in Piteå is northern Sweden's most significant former psychiatric hospital landscape — opened in 1893 as Piteå Hospital och Asyl, designed by Medicinalstyrelsen architect Axel Kumlien on Pitholmen, and for nearly a century the central institution for Upper Norrland. Thousands of patients passed through; many lived out decades behind its gates in a self-sufficient community of wards, workshops, farms and a landscaped park. A hospital cemetery (from 1898) holds roughly 900–970 burials — staff graves marked, most patient graves unmarked. Psychiatric care wound down around 1987 (centenary closure often dated 1993); today Furunäset Hotell och Konferens and a business village occupy the monumental brick complex. Guests and staff report shadows, footsteps and a watched feeling; TV paranormal programmes have filmed here. Haunted Sweden centres documented medical and social history — including isolation cells and long-term confinement — and treats ghost claims as anecdote. Walk the grounds; join Guidning i galenskapen / Journey into Madness when offered; book the hotel officially and respect patients' memory.
places.whyItFitsHauntedSweden: Flagship Norrbotten dark-heritage site: 100 years of documented psychiatric care, nationally noted kulturmiljö, overnight hotel in former wards, patient cemetery, therapeutic park and pine waterfront, guided history storytelling (Journey into Madness). Visual 9.5/10, historical value 10/10, dark history 10/10, folklore strength 8.5/10, paranormal reputation 8.5/10 — Haunted Sweden Score 9.5. Premium content potential EXTREMELY HIGH; research confidence HIGH. Ideal verification mission: overnight, cemetery and park photography, Journey into Madness tour, archive research with ethical care, compare folklore with Piteå Museum / kulturmiljö sources.
places.shortDescription: Piteå's 1893 Hospital och Asyl — Kumlien brick complex, patient cemetery and park, now hotel and conference amid Norrbotten pines.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Furunäset (historically Piteå hospital och asyl; later Furunäsets sjukhus) occupies Belonasvängen / Furunäset on western Pitholmen, Piteå, Norrbotten. FOUNDATION: Riksdag central-hospital policy from 1823; Serafimerordensgillet plan 1873 proposed care for Västerbotten–Norrbotten. In 1886 Medicinalstyrelsen director August Almén and architect Axel Kumlien surveyed sites; Pitholmen was chosen for ground, water, food supply and shelter from winds. Construction 1890–1893 (builder contract 1889); inaugurated 1893. First patient transfers included steamer arrivals of men and women from overcrowded hospitals elsewhere in Sweden (late October 1893 often cited). HOSPITAL vs ASYL: Under the 1858 Hospitalstadga, "hospital" meant a curative course institution; "asyl" meant long-term care for those judged incurable — both functions shared the same Piteå buildings. ARCHITECTURE: Axel Kumlien (Medicinalstyrelsen's hospital specialist; also Uppsala/Ulleråker, Kristinehamn/Marieberg, Lund/S:t Lars among others) designed a closed four-wing brick complex around a rectangular courtyard ("Borgen"), adapted to the northern climate; originally two storeys, third floor added 1927–30. Separate male/female wards; isolation and "storm" (agitated) departments; hospital church hall (now assembly space). Originally dozens of isolation cells (kulturmiljö sources cite on the order of 80+ isolationsrum). COMMUNITY & PARK: Large landscaped grounds in English-park tradition (grotto feature; later Belonaparken); farms, gardens, workshops and cold bathing supported a largely self-sufficient institutional economy and nature-oriented daily order. Cemetery laid out 1898; roughly 900–970 people buried (local tallies ~962–967) — staff memorial stones; patients largely unmarked. Peak mid-20th century around 800 patients. TREATMENTS (period medical practice): isolation and cell confinement; prolonged baths (långbad); later bed treatment, psychosurgery era and psychopharmacology (hibernal and related drugs quieting wards — remembered in local guided history). Third-party care on surrounding farms for capable patients. CLOSURE & REUSE: Large-scale psychiatric activity left around 1987; centenary/official end often given as 1993. Redeveloped as Furunäset Hotell och Konferens and företagsby (business village) while retaining high kulturhistoriskt value (Piteå Museum kulturmiljö analysis). DARK HISTORY (documented social/medical context — not paranormal claims): long-term forced institutionalisation; isolation wards; patients who remained for decades (media and tours highlight Anna Lindersson, admitted 1893, died 1960 — presented as among Sweden's longest involuntary confinements; diagnose details in press are secondary and journals remain partly sealed); deaths on site; cemetery of the forgotten; stigma of mental illness; hierarchical staff–patient life. Haunted Sweden approaches this as heritage of care and suffering, not entertainment at patients' expense.
places.legend: FOLKLORE & MEDIA REPUTATION (not scientifically verified): Popular lists and local press call Furunäset one of Sweden's most haunted places, largely because of its asylum past. Anecdotes include shadow figures, footsteps in empty corridors, unexplained voices, feeling watched, cold spots and odd sounds in former wards and basements. Hotel guests and staff (including past owners quoted in Piteå-Tidningen) describe peripheral vision sightings and sensing someone who is not there. TV series Det okända filmed on site; SVT and local media have covered the haunted reputation alongside history. Museum educators have noted that many "ghost" stories cluster in basements — areas patients historically used least — a useful reminder to question folklore geography. GUIDED EXPERIENCES (documented cultural programming): "Guidning i galenskapen" / "Journey into Madness" — seasonal storytelling walking tour (Elin Johansson / Wabi-sabi via Visit Piteå), ~45 minutes from the marina by Heta Hyttan to the old patient cemetery, covering institutional history, care methods and individual fates. This is historical interpretation of a difficult past, not an official paranormal guarantee. Separate folklore ghost walks may be offered by storytellers; verify current programmes. SPECIAL AREAS: main hospital building (Borgen); former isolation / storm-cell corridors; historic park; cemetery; pine forest and Piteälven waterfront. ATMOSPHERE: Monumental brick, courtyard, park paths, ancient pines, quiet riverside — one of Sweden's strongest former-asylum environments. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight hotel stay; Journey into Madness; cemetery documentation with respect; park EVP only where permitted; history vs folklore; mental-healthcare timeline. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, early morning mist. Keep DOCUMENTED hospital history separate from WITNESS anecdotes and media folklore above.
places.safetyNote: Active hotel, conference centre and business village — book lodging only through official Furunäset Hotell channels. Respect private offices, residents and restricted wings. Cemetery and park: quiet, respectful behaviour; do not disturb graves or memorials. Guided history tours are bookable seasonally (Visit Piteå / Wabi-sabi); do not force entry to closed storm cells or basements. Night investigation only with permission; treat the site as a place of former patients' lives, not a thrill playground.
places.shortDescriptionSv: Piteås hospital och asyl från 1893 — Kumliens tegelkomplex, patientkyrkogård och park, idag hotell och konferens i norrbottnisk tallskog.
places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Furunäset (Piteå hospital och asyl; senare Furunäsets sjukhus), Pitholmen, Piteå. Platsval 1886 (Almén & Axel Kumlien); bygge 1890–93; invigt 1893. Hospital (botbara) och asyl (långvård) enligt 1858 års Hospitalsstadga i samma hus. Fyrlängad »Borgen«, tredje våning 1927–30. Isoleringsrum/stormavdelning; park, jordbruk, verkstäder; kyrkogård från 1898 (~900–970 begravda, patienter ofta omärkta). Topp ca 800 patienter. Behandlingar i tidens praxis: isolering, långbad, senare psykokirurgi/psykofarmaka. Psykiatrisk verksamhet avvecklad ca 1987 (jubileum/stängning ofta 1993). Idag hotell, konferens och företagsby — högt kulturhistoriskt värde (Piteå museum). Mörk historia: långvarig tvångsvård, isolering, dödsfall, stigma — inte spökbevis.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE & MEDIA: Ofta kallad en av Sveriges mest hemsökta platser. Vittnesmål: skuggor, fotsteg, röster, känsla av att bli iakttagen, köld. Det okända m.fl. har filmat. GUIDNING: Guidning i galenskapen / Journey into Madness (~45 min) till patientkyrkogården — historieberättelse, inte bevis för spöken. OMRÅDEN: Borgen, isoleringskorridorer, park, kyrkogård, tallskog/älv.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Furunäset i Piteå är norra Sveriges viktigaste tidigare sinnessjukhusmiljö — invigd 1893 som Piteå hospital och asyl efter Axel Kumliens ritningar, upptagningsområde Övre Norrland i nästan hundra år. Tusentals patienter; kyrkogård med omkring tusen gravar; park och självförsörjande institutionsliv. Idag hotell och företagsby. Gäst- och personalberättelser om skuggor och fotsteg samt guidningen Guidning i galenskapen hålls isär från dokumenterad vårdhistoria. Boka officiellt; visa respekt för dem som levde och dog här.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt hotell, konferens och företagsby – boka endast via officiella kanaler. Respektera kontor, boende och stängda längor. Kyrkogård och park: tystnad och respekt; rör inte gravar. Historieguidningar bokas säsongsvis; tvinga dig inte in i stormceller eller källare. Nattutredning endast med tillstånd. Platsen är före detta patienters livsmiljö — inte en thrillpark.

places.name: Home Hotel Victoria
places.englishName: Home Hotel Victoria (Victoriahemmet / Clarion Collection Hotel Victoria)
places.address: F. E. Elmgrens gata 5, 553 16 Jönköping, Sweden
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Home Hotel Victoria in central Jönköping occupies an English-inspired building completed around 1882 on the initiative of philanthropist, writer and care pioneer Ebba Ramsay (1828–1922). Known historically as Viktoria / Victoriahemmet, the house combined social and religious mission work with a temperance (alcohol-free) inn and a large assembly hall — part of Ramsay's wider Jönköping legacy that also includes Wilhelmsro children's care outside town. Later uses included a school and Sveriges Radio before hotel conversion (Clarion Collection / today Home Hotel Victoria under Strawberry), with décor nodding to the city's matchstick industry. Folklore — amplified by Strawberry's haunted-hotels series — says Ebba never left: Room 426 on the attic floor is the classic hotspot, with guests reporting a calm presence sitting on the bed edge, soft footsteps and rustling. Haunted Sweden separates Ramsay's documented philanthropy from witness anecdotes. Book officially; ask for 426 if available.
places.whyItFitsHauntedSweden: Authentic 1880s philanthropic landmark; unique Ebba Ramsay connection; owners openly market "Jönköping's kindest ghost"; Room 426 overnight investigation; Strawberry haunted-hotel series companion to Bilan and Grand Helsingborg; central accessibility. Visual 9/10, historical value 9/10, folklore strength 9.5/10, paranormal reputation 9/10, overnight potential 10/10 — Haunted Sweden Score 9.4. Premium content potential VERY HIGH; research confidence HIGH. Ideal verification mission: overnight in 426, attic EVP with permission, staff interviews, compare hotel lore with SBL/Wilhelmsro vs Victoria building history.
places.shortDescription: Jönköping's 1882 Victoriahemmet — Ebba Ramsay's historic house, now Home Hotel Victoria, famous for the gentle Room 426 legend.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Home Hotel Victoria stands at F. E. Elmgrens gata 5, Jönköping (Småland), in the Väster district near Sofiakyrkan and the matchstick-museum quarter. EBBA RAMSAY: Ebba Gustafva Ramsay (née Karström, 1 Oct 1828 Stockholm – 29 Oct 1922 Jönköping) was a writer, translator, artist and philanthropist — among Sweden's early Sunday-school pioneers, founder of day-care for working mothers' children in Jönköping, organiser of archipelago health colonies, and a national figure in care for disabled and epileptic children centred on Wilhelmsro (Vilhelmsro) outside Jönköping (father's farm bought 1872; Hoppet asylum 1878; later epilepsy-focused homes). THE VICTORIA BUILDING: On Ramsay's initiative the Viktoria / Victoriahemmet property was built in stages about 1877–1882 (often summarised as 1882) by Gothenburg architect J. A. Westerberg in English-inspired architecture. Contemporary descriptions (e.g. Smålands Allehanda 1882) emphasise a large assembly hall (Viktoriasalen, ~400 seats) for prayers, lectures and civic events, reading rooms, guest rooms and an alcohol-free temperance inn (nykterhetsvärdshus) — Ramsay also published on temperance inns and alcoholism as society's "cancer." Hotel and tourism texts often describe Victoriahemmet as a home for vulnerable children (epilepsy / intellectual disability / children without stable support). Haunted Sweden notes that Ramsay's best-documented institutional children's care was at Wilhelmsro, and that popular hotel histories sometimes blend the town Victoria building with that wider philanthropic programme; both belong to her Jönköping legacy. LATER USES: School use from the early 1900s (Myling and local summaries cite ~1903); Sveriges Radio mid-20th century; hotel operation from the 1990s as Clarion Collection Hotel Victoria, later rebranded Home Hotel Victoria (Strawberry). Expansions and renovations (incl. ~38 new rooms ~2021; attic-floor works affecting rooms 426–428) while retaining historic character and match-industry decorative motifs. DARK HISTORY CONTEXT: Care for sick, disabled and socially vulnerable children in 19th-century institutions implies ordinary illness and death among residents and staff over decades — not automatic hauntings. Temperance work responded to documented alcohol harm. Keep philanthropy and building chronology separate from Room 426 folklore below.
places.legend: FOLKLORE — EBBA RAMSAY / ROOM 426 (not scientifically verified): Local and hotel tradition holds that Ebba Ramsay never truly left the building she founded. The attic floor — especially Room 426 (also 427 and 428 in staff/PR accounts) — is the primary hotspot. Guests report waking to the sensation that someone sat on the bed edge; soft footsteps; rustling as if on newspaper on the floor; objects moving; quiet whispers; cold spots; feeling watched. Staff and Strawberry materials generally describe the presence as calm and protective — "Jönköping's kindest ghost" — rather than frightening. During renovations, hotel management jokingly "relocated" Ebba to an "Ebba suite" while attic rooms were refurbished (PR storytelling, not evidence). WITNESS & MEDIA: Strawberry's haunted-hotels feature "The benefactress"; JKPG tourism copy; Myling and press interviews with directors citing guest and cleaner experiences (e.g. vacuum attachment allegedly moving). A medium is said to have been invited after repeated reports. SPECIAL AREAS: Room 426; attic floor; historic staircase; atrium / light courtyard (ljusgård) dining heart. ATMOSPHERE: 1882 architecture, elegant atrium, quiet upper floors after midnight, match-industry décor — classic overnight haunted-hotel setting. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight in 426; attic EVP with permission; history vs folklore (Victoria vs Wilhelmsro); staff interviews; Haunted Sweden overnight challenge. BEST CONDITIONS: overnight stay, rainy evenings, winter darkness, quiet weekdays. Keep DOCUMENTED Ramsay philanthropy separate from FOLKLORE and anecdotes above.
places.safetyNote: Active hotel — book only through official Home Hotel Victoria / Strawberry channels. Respect guests, staff, fire rules and night quiet. Do not film or investigate in corridors or other guests' rooms without permission; Room 426 (and attic rooms) depend on availability. Lobby and restaurant are public-facing but still respect privacy.
places.shortDescriptionSv: Jönköpings Victoriahemmet från 1882 — Ebba Ramsays historiska hus, idag Home Hotel Victoria, känt för den milda legenden om rum 426.
places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Home Hotel Victoria, F. E. Elmgrens gata 5, Jönköping. Ebba Ramsay (1828–1922) — författare, filantrop, pionjär inom barn- och epilepsivård (Wilhelmsro m.m.). Viktoria/Victoriahemmet uppfört ca 1877–1882 (arkitekt J. A. Westerberg), engelskinspirerat: temperancevärdshus, Viktoriasalen (~400 platser), social-religiös verksamhet. Hotelltexter beskriver ofta barnhem för utsatta/epilepsi — Haunted Sweden noterar att Ramsays mest dokumenterade barnsjukvård låg på Wilhelmsro och att populära hotellberättelser ibland blandar platserna. Senare skola (~1903), Sveriges Radio, hotell från 1990-talet (Clarion Collection → Home Hotel Victoria). Renoveringar/utbyggnad med bevarad karaktär och tändsticksdekor. Håll isär från rum 426-folklore.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE: Ebba Ramsay sägs aldrig ha lämnat huset — rum 426 (även 427–428) på vinden. Gäster: någon sätter sig på sängkanten, mjuka fotsteg, prassel, föremål, köld, känsla av att bli iakttagen. Personal/Strawberry: lugn, skyddande närvaro — »Jönköpings snällaste spöke«. VITTNESMÅL & MEDIA: Strawberry haunted hotels, JKPG, Myling. OMRÅDEN: 426, vind, trappa, ljusgård.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Home Hotel Victoria i Jönköping ligger i Ebba Ramsays Viktoriahemmet från ca 1882 — temperancevärdshus, samlingssal och social mission, senare skola, radio och hotell. Folklore säger att Ebba aldrig checkade ut, särskilt rum 426 på vinden, med lugna gästupplevelser som Strawberry lyfter fram. Haunted Sweden skiljer Ramsays dokumenterade filantropi (inkl. Wilhelmsro) från vittnesmål. Boka officiellt; önska 426 om det finns.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt hotell – boka endast via officiella kanaler (Home Hotel Victoria / Strawberry). Respektera gäster, personal, brandskydd och nattlig tystnad. Filma eller utred inte i korridorer eller andras rum utan tillstånd; rum 426 och vindsvåning beror på tillgång. Lobby och restaurang är öppna men respektera privatliv.

places.name: Wiks Slott
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Wiks Slott (Viks slott) on Lårstaviken south-west of Uppsala is one of Sweden's best-preserved medieval castles — estate roots in the 1200s, a late-1400s stone fortress, and today a Region Uppsala hotel, conference venue and folk high school. Documented history runs from Israel And and Ramborg Israelsdotter through the Vasa siege of 1521 and Scholander's 1858–60 restoration. Folklore, presented on Region Uppsala's own heritage points and Visit Sweden, is exceptionally rich: the White Lady often identified with Anna von der Grünau (d. 1612 on the Mälaren ice), Fru Ramborg when the clock strikes thirteen, a giant woman by the shoreline, and an armoured presence climbing from cellar to library. Haunted Sweden keeps building and ownership records separate from these legends. Book overnight lodging; walk the park and shore in fog.
places.whyItFitsHauntedSweden: Flagship Uppland haunted castle hotel: finest mid-Sweden medieval borg authenticity, officially featured Region Uppsala ghost traditions (White Lady / Fru Ramborg), multiple named legends, overnight accommodation, Mälaren photography. Visual 10/10, historical value 10/10, architectural value 10/10, folklore strength 10/10, paranormal reputation 9.5/10, overnight investigation potential 10/10 — Haunted Sweden Score 9.7. Premium content potential EXTREMELY HIGH; research confidence HIGH. Ideal verification mission: overnight, library EVP with permission, White Lady park/shore documentation, interview staff, compare folklore with Wikipedia/Region Uppsala/family-chronicle notes, documentary episode.
places.shortDescription: Medieval Wik by Mälaren — late-1400s fortress hotel famous for the White Lady (Anna von der Grünau) and Fru Ramborg legends.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Wiks / Viks slott at Viks Mur 29, Balingsta socken, Uppsala municipality (Uppland), on Lårstaviken (Ekoln / Lake Mälaren), ~20 km SW of Uppsala. Owned by Region Uppsala since 1923 (former landsting); folk high school, hotel/conference, restaurant/café; byggnadsminne (KML; commonly 1982). Map note: verified coordinates ~59.736 N, 17.462 E (Balingsta shoreline) — not central Uppsala. EARLY ESTATE: Lagman Israel Andreasson (And), d. 1289. Vik recorded 1303 for Ramborg Israelsdotter (And) and 1315 for husband Arvid Gustavsson (Sparre av Vik), killed at Nyköpings gästabud 1317. Inheritance via Sparre/Bielke; many women as owners. STONE CASTLE: Late 1400s enkelhusborg associated with Klaus Nilsson / Katarina Stensdotter till Wik / Nils Klausson (Sparre av Ellinge) — grey-stone lower levels, monk-bond brick above, deep undercrofts. WAR: Peder Swart — Gustav Vasa besieged Vik 1521 for more than a year (defender Knut Nilsson). REBUILDS: Mid-1600s Gustaf Horn / Sigrid Bielke works (stair, baroque portal); Fredrik Wilhelm Scholander 1858–1860 gave present exterior and Riddarsalen. Continuous inheritance until sale 1912; Region 1923. Park: baroque and English traces; bathing shore. ANNA VON DER GRÜNAU (documented person; death narrative): German-born court lady (née von der Grünau), married Berndt Didrik Mörner 1605, widow 1610, connected to Wik in the early 1600s. Family/local chronicle tradition holds she died winter 1612 travelling over Mälaren ice toward Skokloster (friend Margareta Wrangel) when the sledge broke through — Region Uppsala summarises she was found "dead and frozen." Treat chronicle drowning as historical tradition; treat witch-refusal-to-rescue embellishments and the subsequent ghost as folklore (see legend). DARK HISTORY CONTEXT: siege, noble deaths, lakeside isolation, aristocratic tragedies — not automatic hauntings.
places.legend: FOLKLORE — THE WHITE LADY / ANNA VON DER GRÜNAU (Region Uppsala heritage point "Den vita frun på Wik"): One of Wik's best-known ghosts — a white-clad woman in mist on the castle, courtyard and park, sometimes leaving wet footprints; winter nights, desperate cries from the lake. Tradition identifies her with Anna von der Grünau after the 1612 ice accident. Embellished tellings add that onlookers mistook her floating skirts for witchcraft and fled; folklore also says she seeks her children. Haunted Sweden separates the chronicle drowning tradition from apparition claims. FOLKLORE — FRU RAMBORG: Visit Sweden and local lore — when the castle clock strikes thirteen her pale face appears in a tower window; troll-treasure tale of wealth; digital heritage app presents her as lingering guardian. Historical Ramborg Israelsdotter (early 1300s; Västeråker copper grave slab) is real — clock-thirteen sightings are folklore. FOLKLORE — THE GIANT WOMAN: Enormous female figure in floor-length cloak and tricorne hat in the park or rising from the inlet (SR P4 / staff anecdotes). FOLKLORE — THE ARMOURED KNIGHT: Heavy footsteps from the cellar up a hidden staircase (lönntrappa) into the library — as if armour walked. OTHER: White/Black Ladies; chairs scraping; courtyard shadows; corner-tower light that returns after lock-up (Visit Sweden). WITNESS REPORTS (anecdotal): Guests and staff — cold spots, shadows, footsteps, sounds, lights; managers have publicly discussed unexplained attic lights. SPECIAL AREAS: library (knight); cellars; hidden staircase; castle park (White Lady); shoreline (Giant Woman / Anna cries). ATMOSPHERE: Medieval towers, thick stone, fog over Mälaren fields — premier overnight haunted-castle setting. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight; White Lady park/shore; thirteenth-bell Fru Ramborg; library EVP with permission; history vs folklore. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, overnight. Keep DOCUMENTED history separate from FOLKLORE above.
places.safetyNote: Active Region Uppsala hotel, folk high school and conference site — book lodging and meals through official Wiks slott / Region Uppsala channels. Respect course participants, staff and closed floors. Cellars, library and secret stairs are not free-roam zones; access only when permitted. Park, trails and bathing area: stay on paths, watch water edges in dark/fog. No unauthorized night investigation inside the castle.
places.shortDescriptionSv: Medeltida Wik vid Lårstaviken — senmedeltida stenborg, Region Uppsala-hotell och Fru Ramborgs spöklegender.
places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Wiks/Viks slott, Viks Mur 29, Balingsta — Lårstaviken. Region Uppsala sedan 1923; byggnadsminne. Koordinater ~59.736, 17.462 (ej Uppsala centrum). Israel And (d. 1289); Ramborg Israelsdotter 1303; Arvid dödad Nyköping 1317. Borg sent 1400-tal. Gustav Vasa belägrade 1521 >1 år. Horn/Bielke 1600-tal; Scholander 1858–60. Anna von der Grünau: historisk hovdam, änka 1610; släktkrönika om drunkning/frysning på Mälaris 1612 mot Skokloster — håll isär från spökpåståenden.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE: Vita frun — vitklädd i dimma, våta fotspår, skrik från sjön; knyts till Anna von der Grünau efter 1612 (Region Uppsala). Fru Ramborg — ansikte i torn när klockan slår tretton; trollskatt. Jättekvinna vid strand/park. Rustning: steg källare–lönntrappa–bibliotek. VITTNESMÅL: köld, skuggor, ljud, lampor. OMRÅDEN: bibliotek, källare, lönntrappa, park, strand.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Wiks slott vid Lårstaviken är en av Sveriges bäst bevarade medeltidsborgar — 1200-talsanor, stenborg sent 1400-tal, Region Uppsala-hotell. Folklore (Region Uppsala/Visit Sweden): Vita frun ofta knuten till Anna von der Grünau (isolycka 1612), Fru Ramborg när klockan slår tretton, jättekvinna vid stranden och rustningssteg till biblioteket. Haunted Sweden skiljer dokumenterad historia från legend. Boka övernattning; gå park och strand i dimma.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt Region Uppsala-hotell, folkhögskola och konferens – boka via officiella kanaler. Respektera kursdeltagare och stängda våningar. Källare, bibliotek och lönntrappor endast med tillstånd. Park och bad: håll dig till stigar, var försiktig vid vatten i mörker/dimma. Ingen otillåten nattutredning inne i borgen.

places.name: Görvälns Slott
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Görvälns Slott sits on a bay of Lake Mälaren inside Görväln Nature Reserve in Järfälla — one of Stockholm County's most scenic castle hotels. The estate is documented from the late Middle Ages (name from the 1460s; Uppsala diocese farms, then crown land). In 1571 Johan III donated Görväln to Antonius de Palma. The present Gotland-sandstone manor rose 1659–1675 for Elsa Elisabeth Brahe (widow of Erik Axelsson Oxenstierna), completed under her second husband Duke Adolf Johan of Pfalz-Zweibrücken; Jean de la Vallée is the probable architect (Nicodemus Tessin the Elder is also named in some museum texts). An English-style park, Carlsköld lime avenue, Salin-era exotic trees and a municipal arboretum (1980s) frame the lakeside façades. Järfälla Municipality bought the land in 1963 and the buildings in 1967; after restorations the house reopened as a boutique hotel and restaurant (major renovation 2008). Unlike Wik or Häringe, Görväln has no single famous named ghost in official tourism or regional ghost guides — atmosphere, noble tragedy and informal guest talk about footsteps, cold spots and a watched feeling carry the mystery. Haunted Sweden keeps verified Brahe–Adolf Johan building history separate from unproven apparition stories. Book overnight; walk the public park and reserve; respect hotel and private areas.

places.history: DOCUMENTED: Görvälns slott (also Görwäln) is a former säteri in Järfälla socken, Stockholm County, on the Görväln bay of Lake Mälaren inside Görvälns naturreservat. It is a protected byggnadsminne (Länsstyrelsen Stockholm lists Görvälns gård among county heritage sites). MEDIEVAL–REFORMATION: Earliest known owner tradition reaches the late 1300s/early 1400s (Nils Jönsson Oxenstierna). The name Görväln is documented from the 1460s as two farms under Uppsala diocese (later bishop's farms tied to Almare-Stäket). After the Reformation (1520s) the estate became crown land until 1571, when Johan III donated it to the Italian nobleman Antonius de Palma (some popular texts say Polish — Wikipedia: Italian). Son Scipio de Palma transferred it in 1605 to Chancellor Svante Bielke, who rebuilt a säteri lower on the slope ("Stora röda byggnaden"). Inheritance passed through Bielke to Elsa Elisabeth Brahe (1632–1689) in 1643. BAROQUE CASTLE: Erik Axelsson Oxenstierna decided on a new main house; after his death in 1656, Elsa Elisabeth (widow at 25 with five young children) contracted Axel Sparre in 1659 for a Gotland-stone house. Works 1659–1661 under hovingenjör Johan Peter Kirstenius; architect most often given as Jean de la Vallée (Tessin the Elder also mentioned in Stockholms läns museum — treat as disputed attribution). Duke Adolf Johan of Pfalz-Zweibrücken (Karl X Gustav's brother), Elsa's second husband from 1661, dismissed the builder and work stalled ~15 years; the house was largely finished only ~1675. Entrance faces the lake — waterways as important as roads. Wings frame the courtyard toward Mälaren. Baroque garden sculpture commissions (hollow beläten for water) are documented for Elsa Elisabeth. LATER ESTATE: Heirs of Adolf Johan faced severe debt; Stegeborg was seized but Görväln, as Elsa's property, was kept. Later owners include Herman Witte, Pehr Carlsköld (1750s — lime avenue toward Görvälns krog; interior modernisation), Adolf Rudbeck, Bengt Magnus Björkman (from 1802 — attic storey and farm buildings), Mauritz Salin (1903–1927 — exotic lakeside trees; glass verandah and kitchen wing 1901 era additions), then municipal ownership. PARK & ARBORETUM: Today's park largely follows an 1869 proposal — English landscape character toward the lake and a more formal garden east. Exotic plantings under Salin; Järfälla Municipality developed the arboretum in the 1980s (100+ species; not an 1800s municipal arboretum). Agriculture still shapes the valley. MODERN: Land purchased 1963 for outdoor recreation; buildings 1967; restorations 1980s and total hotel renovation 2008; boutique hotel, restaurant and conference under private operators (Eklund family among recent lessees) with rooms in wings and villas. Nature reserve (formalised 1995) stretches along Mälaren between Hässelby and Kallhäll. DARK HISTORY (documented only): Erik Oxenstierna's death before the new house rose; Elsa's widowhood and five minors; stalled construction and court/rank conflicts around Adolf Johan; heirs' near-bankruptcy; infant death of Anna Catharina Witte at Görväln (1720); Hedvig Witte's death in childbirth (1741); noble-family isolation and servant/farm-worker life on a large Mälaren estate — tragedy and hardship, not proof of hauntings. Do not invent crimes or imprisonments not in the record.
places.legend: FOLKLORE vs PUBLISHED RECORD: Reliable Swedish sources (Wikipedia, Järfälla kommun, Stockholms läns museum, Länsstyrelsen, official hotel site) do NOT preserve a single nationally famous named ghost for Görväln comparable to Wik's White Lady or Häringe's Spökafton cast. Haunted Sweden therefore does not invent a "White Lady of Görväln" as documented tradition. ATMOSPHERIC & INFORMAL LORE (unverified): As with many Swedish manor hotels, visitors and staff sometimes speak of a heavy presence in historic salons, phantom footsteps on the grand staircase or empty corridors, doors that seem to move, cold spots, shadow impressions, and a watched feeling after dark — especially when mist rises from Mälaren over the English park and arboretum. Female-apparition motifs appear in general Swedish castle folklore and may be casually attached to Brahe-era women in oral retellings; treat any such naming as speculative folklore, not archival fact. Park and shoreline walks after sunset fuel nature-reserve ghost talk (figures among oaks, sounds from the bay) without a fixed local legend text in municipal guides. WITNESS REPORTS: Anecdotal guest/staff experiences only; no widely cited scientific investigation or official regional "ghost story" page for Görväln was located in this research pass. SPECIAL AREAS (atmosphere + informal reports): (1) Historic main building / salons — Baroque fabric, hotel public rooms. (2) Grand staircase — often cited in generic manor-ghost storytelling. (3) Castle park — 1869 English layout, mist, ancient trees. (4) Arboretum — quiet, exotic plantings, mysterious dusk light. (5) Lakeside grounds — photography and folklore setting. ATMOSPHERE: Sandstone façades over Mälaren, thick historic rooms, staircase, oak and lime avenues, fog over fields, boutique-hotel quiet after midnight. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight stay; park after dark (public paths); EVP in historic salons with hotel permission; history vs folklore; staff interviews; sunrise/sunset photography. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, heavy fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, overnight. Keep DOCUMENTED Brahe–Adolf Johan / municipal history separate from FOLKLORE and anecdotal reports above.

places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Görvälns slott, tidigare säteri i Järfälla socken, vid Görvälnsfjärden i Mälaren i Görvälns naturreservat; byggnadsminne. Medeltida anor; namnet från 1460-talet (Uppsala stift); kronan efter reformationen; 1571 donerade Johan III till Antonius de Palma. Via Bielke till Elsa Elisabeth Brahe (1632–1689). Nuvarande huvudbyggnad i gotländsk sandsten 1659–1675; troligen Jean de la Vallée (Tessin d.ä. nämns i vissa museitexter). Erik Axelsson Oxenstierna dog 1656; Elsa änka med fem barn; andra maken hertig Adolf Johan; bygget låg nere ~15 år. Engelsk park enligt förslag 1869; lindallé Carlsköld 1750-tal; exotiska träd under Mauritz Salin; kommunalt arboretum 1980-tal. Mark 1963, byggnader 1967 till Järfälla kommun; hotellrenovering 2008. Mörk dokumenterad historia: änkeskap, skuld hos arvingar, spädbarnsdöd 1720, död i barnsäng 1741 — inte spökbevis. OBS: Stockholms läns museum skriver felaktigt Ebba Brahe; korrekt byggherre är Elsa Elisabeth Brahe.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE vs KÄLLOR: Wikipedia, Järfälla kommun, läns museum, hotellets sajt och Länsstyrelsen ger ingen etablerad namngiven spökfigur för Görväln (till skillnad från Wik/Häringe). INFORMELL LORE: gäster/personal kan tala om fotsteg, köld, skuggor, dörrar och känsla av att bli iakttagen i salonger och trapphus; park/strand i dimma. Kvinnliga vålnadsmotiv i allmän svensk slottsfolklore bör inte kopplas till Brahe som fastställd lokal legend utan belägg. Inga vida citerade vetenskapliga undersökningar hittades. OMRÅDEN: huvudbyggnad, trapphus, engelsk park, arboretum, sjösida. Håll isär dokumenterad historia och anekdoter.

Engelsk park, arboretum och naturreservat ger stark atmosfär. Till skillnad från Wik eller Häringe saknas en enda berömd namngiven spöklegend i officiella guider; mystiken bygger på herrgårdsmiljö och informella gästberättelser. places.name: Gimo Herrgård
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Gimo Herrgård in Östhammar municipality is widely presented as Sweden's first fully developed Gustavian manor — Jean Eric Rehn's white plastered stone house with linked wings, finished 1767 beside Gimosjön (Gimodammen) in the historic Gimo Bruk ironworks community. The crown founded a blast furnace here in 1615; Louis De Geer and Walloon expertise built a major Uppland ironworks (De Geer ownership into the mid-1700s). Robert Finlay commissioned Rehn's masterplan; Jean Henri Le Febure completed the estate the year he died. Crescent stables, twin orangeries, French front park and English rear park, Bruksgatan workers' housing and a runestone on the grounds still frame one of Sweden's most coherent bruk environments — byggnadsminne since 1995 (Länsstyrelsen Uppsala). Today it is a four-star hotel, spa (Sjöstugan) and conference venue. Local folklore names a butler "Johansson" under 19th-century owner Carl Reuterskiöld; Countryside Hotels and Petter Inedahl's Spöklikt collect staff/guest stories of cold drafts, lights in empty windows, footsteps and shadow figures. Haunted Sweden keeps Rehn–De Geer industrial history separate from those unverified reports. Book overnight; respect hotel and private areas.

places.shortDescription: 1767 Jean Eric Rehn Gustavian manor hotel at Gimo Bruk — Sweden's first Gustavian estate narrative, ironworks heritage, English park by Gimosjön, and local Johansson butler folklore.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Gimo Herrgård is a stone manor in Gimo, Skäfthammar socken, Östhammar municipality (Uppland), at Bruksgatan beside Gimosjön / Gimodammen within the historic Gimo Bruk ironworks environment. EARLY SITE: Village Gimmu mentioned 1375–76; Skäfthammars kyrka (15th c.) nearby; runestone (Uppland Runic Inscription 1132) preserved by the dam/manor grounds. IRONWORKS: Crown blast furnace founded 1615 (Hans Sifversson). From 1627 leased to Willem de Besche and Louis De Geer; after ennoblement De Geer purchased (1643) and expanded to blast furnace and hammers with Walloon ironworkers — part of his Uppland network with Österby and Lövsta. De Geer family held Gimo until 1756. DOCUMENTED DISASTER: A major fire in 1649 at the lower hammer inauguration destroyed much of the works and half of Gimo village; rebuilding followed (vallon.se / local bruk histories). INDUSTRIAL DECLINE CONTEXT: 19th-century competition pushed Gimo toward forestry and sawmilling; blast-furnace operation ended 1936 when Korsnäs AB took over; ironworking tradition cited to ~1945. Gimo bruks AB (1893/94 under Carl Leonard Reuterskiöld); later Gimo–Österby; bankruptcy era mid-1930s. MANOR ARCHITECTURE: Sold 1756 to Scots traders John Jennings and Robert Finlay; Finlay (sole owner by early 1760s) commissioned royal architect Jean Eric Rehn for a new manor and general plan for the whole bruk. In 1764 Finlay sold to East India Company director Jean Henri Le Febure (Lefebure); Rehn's commission continued. Estate completed 1767 — the same year Le Febure died — main house with courtyard framed by two wings; opposite, crescent-shaped stables/coach houses; two contemporary orangeries behind the house. Rehn placed the manor on the old fogde/inspector farm site; French-inspired park toward the front, English landscape park with winding paths to the rear (still readable). Hotel and heritage texts call it Sweden's first fully developed Gustavian manor; Länsstyrelsen Uppsala (byggnadsminne 1995) ranks it among the country's most unified and best-preserved manor ensembles with interiors/painting, and among Rehn's finest works. Park is part of the protected setting (RAÄ guidance cites Gimo as example). Workers' dwellings along Bruksgatan built 1780s (remodelled 1880s); inspector's house early 1700s, enlarged 1760s. OWNERSHIP AFTER: Inherited by Jean Lefebure-Lillienberg; from 1806 Reuterskiöld family (Carl Reuterskiöld associated with 1834–1894 management era in folklore sources). MODERN: Long use as course/conference centre; today family-run four-star hotel (~85 rooms/suites), restaurant, Sjöstugan SPA Lounge, Countryside Hotels member. DARK HISTORY (documented only — do not invent accidents): Extreme social contrast between manor owners and Walloon/bruk workers; dangerous heat, furnaces and hammers inherent to ironworks life; 1649 fire catastrophe; Le Febure's death the year the house finished; 19th–20th century economic crisis, company failure and end of smelting — hardship and class structure, not proof of hauntings. Generic industrial-accident statistics for Gimo's historic hammers are not inventable here without named archival cases.
places.legend: FOLKLORE (not verified history): Local tradition (collected e.g. in Petter Inedahl, Spöklikt, Carlsson 2018 / Skarn) names a butler Johansson said to have served Carl Reuterskiöld (associated with Gimo management c. 1834–1894). Whether Johansson is the source of reported phenomena is explicitly left open in that account. Countryside Hotels marketing adds stories of a former owner who will not leave his life's work, and guests seeing lights glimmer in windows where no one lives. WITNESS REPORTS (anecdotal staff accounts in Inedahl/Skarn — not scientific investigations): In the Vallmosalongen (Poppy Salon), a hidden door to a spiral stair allegedly opened by itself with an icy draft while doors below remained shut and no person was found; feelings of a presence on the narrow stair. Other former staff describe footsteps following room to room; dragging/scraping as of a heavy chest in empty rooms; billiard cues found scattered from their wall rack after a crash; a black human-shaped shadow densifying in an upstairs corner; a silent rolling black orb in the corridor outside the kitchen that vanished when the witness cried out. SPECIAL AREAS: (1) Main manor / historic salons (incl. Vallmosalongen) — original Gustavian character, hotel public rooms. (2) Grand / spiral staircase and service stairs — cold-draft and presence reports. (3) Manor park — English rear park, autumn melancholy under maples. (4) Lakeside / Gimosjön — mist, light on water. (5) Historic ironworks / Bruksgatan — industrial heritage atmosphere (history, not a named ghost walk). ATMOSPHERE: White Gustavian façades, salons, iron-railed double stair to the courtyard, ancient trees, fog over the dam, bruk silence after dark. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight; EVP in salons with permission; night walk Bruksgatan/park; ironworks history vs Johansson folklore; Gimosjön photography. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, heavy fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, overnight. Keep DOCUMENTED Rehn–De Geer–bruk history separate from FOLKLORE and staff anecdotes above.

Interiors, stairs and private wings are not free exploration. Park and bruk streets: stay on public or hotel-permitted areas; do not enter industrial or private buildings. Modern Sandvik facilities nearby are closed workplaces — no trespassing.

places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Gimo herrgård, Östhammars kommun, vid Gimosjön i Gimo bruks miljö; byggnadsminne 1995 (Länsstyrelsen Uppsala). Gimmu 1375–76; kronohytta 1615; Louis De Geer arrende/köp, vallonsmide; De Geer till 1756. Brand 1649 ödelade mycket av bruket och halva byn. Jennings/Finlay; Jean Eric Rehn generalplan och herrgård; Jean Henri Le Febure från 1764; anläggning klar 1767 (samma år Lefebure dog) — huvudbyggnad, flyglar, halvmånestallar, orangerier; fransk park framåt, engelsk park bakåt. En av landets mest enhetliga herrgårdsanläggningar enligt Länsstyrelsen. Arbetarbostäder Bruksgatan 1780-tal. Reuterskiöld 1800-tal; masugn ned 1936; hotell/spa/konferens idag. Mörk dokumenterad historia: klasskillnad, farligt järnarbete, branden 1649, ekonomiska kriser — inte spökbevis.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE: Lokal tradition (t.ex. Petter Inedahl, Spöklikt) om betjänten Johansson under Carl Reuterskiöld (ca 1834–1894). Countryside Hotels: tidigare ägare som inte lämnar; ljus i tomma fönster. VITTNESMÅL (anekdotiska, Skarn/Inedahl): iskall vind och lönndörr i Vallmosalongen/spiraltrappa; fotsteg; släpljud; biljardköer på golvet; svart skuggfigur; svart klot utanför köket. OMRÅDEN: salonger, trapphus, park, Gimosjön, bruksgatan. Håll isär från dokumenterad Rehn-/brukshistoria.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Gimo Herrgård i Östhammar kallas Sveriges första gustavianska herrgård — Jean Eric Rehns vita stenbyggnad med flyglar, klar 1767 vid Gimosjön i Gimo bruk. Kronan grundade hytta 1615; Louis De Geer byggde ut järnbruket med valloner. Finlay beställde Rehns plan; Lefebure fullföljde. Byggnadsminne med orangerier, park och bruksmiljö. Idag hotell, spa och konferens. Folklore om betjänten Johansson och personalberättelser om kölddrag och skuggor hålls isär från dokumenterad industri- och arkitekturhistoria. Boka officiellt.

places.name: Sundbyholms Slott
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Sundbyholms Slott stands on southern Lake Mälaren north of Eskilstuna — a 17th-century stone castle in a landscape that reaches from the Viking Age Sigurdsristningen (Sigurd carving, c. 11th century) to Sweden's first folk school. In the Middle Ages the estate was klostergods of Eskilstuna's Johannite monastery (order established in Eskilstuna c. 1170); after the Reformation it became crown land. In 1597 Duke Karl (later Charles IX) gave it to his illegitimate son, later riksamiral Carl Carlsson Gyllenhielm, who built the present castle 1639–1648 after twelve years as a prisoner of war in Poland. A catastrophic fire at Christmas 1774 gutted the house; it served as barn and store for over 150 years until Eskilstuna restored it (1952–53) as conference and restaurant. Today it is a Green Key castle hotel (lodging in surrounding houses; restaurant and banquets in the castle). Official hotel and local press collect staff and guest stories of a tall dark hooded figure in the wine cellars, rattling keys, self-moving doors and a watched feeling — sometimes linked in folklore to peaceful Gyllenhielm or, more speculatively, Count Cronstedt. Haunted Sweden keeps Vasa–Gyllenhielm building history and the 1774 fire separate from those unverified reports. Book overnight; visit Sigurdsristningen and the nature reserve; respect hotel operations.

places.history: DOCUMENTED: Sundbyholms slott is a stone castle on a Mälaren headland in Eskilstuna municipality (Södermanland), within the Sundbyholm outdoor/nature conservation area (Sundbyholm nature conservation area 1987; nearby Sundbyholmsåsen reserve). VIKING AGE LANDSCAPE: Settlement long before the castle; ~1 km southeast lies Sigurdsristningen (Ramsund carving) — one of Sweden's foremost runic monuments (11th century), depicting the Sigurd Fafnisbane legend and a bridge-building inscription over Ramsundet (Eskilstuna kommun / Länsstyrelsen Södermanland). MEDIEVAL: In the Middle Ages Sundbyholm was monastic estate (klostergods) belonging to Eskilstuna Johanniterkloster. The Johannite order established itself in Eskilstuna around 1170 at Eskil's burial church — the monastery was in Eskilstuna; Sundbyholm was estate land of that house, not a separate monastery founded on this peninsula in 1170. Reformation 1527: Gustav Vasa seized the property for the crown (kungsgård). GYLLENHIELM CASTLE: 1597 Duke Karl (later Charles IX) donated the estate to his illegitimate son Carl Carlsson Gyllenhielm (later riksamiral; half-brother of Gustav II Adolf; grandson of Gustav Vasa). 1615 Kristina Ribbing received Sundbyholm as morning gift. During Gyllenhielm's ~12-year captivity in Poland under cousin Sigismund, the smaller Hertighuset served as manor house. After return he built a representative stone castle 1639–1648 (year 1648 on the northeast portal); he died 1650; widow Kristina moved to Sundbyholm. 1629 he founded Sundby / Gyllenhielmska skolan at his own expense — regarded as Sweden's first folkskola, operating until 1987. After Gyllenhielm (no heir) Seved Bååt raised the house to three storeys (appearance in Suecia Antiqua et Hodierna). Reduktion returned the estate to the crown 1699; 18 crown tenants until 1939. FIRE 1774: Severe fire on/around Christmas Eve 1774 under tenant Captain Adam Jakob von Schoting — sparks from chimneys ignited a newly tarred shingle roof; combustible interiors destroyed, some inner walls collapsed (hotel archive details: wife Brita Liljehök at home; staff discovered fire in attic/roof). Without funds for full rebuild the ruin served as barn and magazine for ~150 years. MODERN: Eskilstuna bought 1939; building-historical survey then restoration 1952–53 as conference venue — 17th-century cellars retained; upper floors adapted (large Riddarsalen partly due to not restoring original room plan). Today hotel (~117 rooms in estate buildings — official site: no overnight rooms inside the castle itself), restaurant, banquets, conference; Green Key. Prince Eugén painted Det gamla slottet here in 1893. DARK HISTORY (documented only): Gyllenhielm's long POW imprisonment; childless death; reduktion loss; 1774 catastrophe and century-and-a-half of degradation; Schoting-era hardship — not proof of hauntings. Hotel folklore also mentions Count Nils August Cronstedt (tenant after 1779; sentenced for insubordination, death sentence commuted by Gustav III to life imprisonment, later freed by Duke Karl) — his later misfortunes are historical; linking him to the hooded cellar figure is speculation.
places.legend: FOLKLORE & HOTEL TRADITION (not scientifically verified): Sundbyholms Slott publishes an official ghosts page and is covered in Ekuriren's Sörmländska spöken series. Staff and guests report a constant feeling of presence; doors opening/closing; keys rattling in empty rooms; handles pressed down alone — especially when new staff start. A peaceful haunting is sometimes linked to Carl Carlsson Gyllenhielm (anecdotes of him selling cannons to feed his men) — if the ghost is Gyllenhielm, hotel lore says it is friendly. Medium Jörgen Gustavsson visited autumn 2008; staff emphasize his closing line: "Here there are only kind ghosts" (medium claim, not evidence). WITNESS REPORTS (hotel / press — anecdotal): Restaurant manager Maria's account after a Viking dinner: locked the castle, went to the wine cellar, heard footsteps thought to be the toastmaster, called twice with no answer, then saw a tall dark figure entirely in black with a hood hiding the face walk through the vault, notice her, pass into another room — empty when followed, only a watched feeling. Hotel site also wonders whether the male cellar figure could be Count Cronstedt (see history — speculative). Guests in the Herrgård reported dragging sounds and creaking stairs when they believed themselves alone (summer 2007) — the hotel itself later notes the receptionist realised late drop-in guests had occupied the suite above (natural explanation for that anecdote). Other popular/media pieces add cold cellars, voices, object movement in breakfast kitchen — treat as unverified. SPECIAL AREAS: (1) Historic wine cellars / vaults — hooded figure report. (2) Castle corridors — footsteps, presence. (3) Historic salons / restaurant floors — guest experiences. (4) Castle park — oaks, mist, Mälaren. (5) Entrance / service areas — door and key phenomena. Nearby Sigurdsristningen is atmospheric archaeology, not a hotel ghost site. ATMOSPHERE: Baroque stone castle, cellars, park, marina, fog over Mälaren, Viking Age carving nearby. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight; EVP in cellars with permission; park night walk; Sigurd stone after sunset (respect site); history vs folklore; Gyllenhielm research. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, heavy fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, overnight. Keep DOCUMENTED Gyllenhielm / 1774 fire history separate from FOLKLORE and witness reports above.
places.safetyNote: Active castle hotel, restaurant and conference venue — book only via official Sundbyholms Slott channels. Overnight rooms are in estate buildings, not inside the historic castle (restaurant/banquets). Respect guests, staff, fire rules and night quiet. Cellars and private areas only with hotel access. Sigurdsristningen and Sundbyholm nature areas are publicly visitable — stay on paths, do not damage the runic carving. Do not trespass closed buildings or marina private zones.
places.shortDescriptionSv: Gyllenhielms slott 1639–1648 vid Mälaren — Sigurdsristningen, branden 1774, Sveriges första folkskola och hotellets berättelser om huva-gestalt i vinkällaren.
places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Sundbyholms slott, Eskilstuna, vid Mälaren i Sundbyholms frilufts-/naturvårdsområde. Vikingatida landskap; Sigurdsristningen ca 1 km SO (1000-tal). Medeltida klostergods under Eskilstuna johanniterkloster (orden i Eskilstuna ca 1170 — inte kloster grundat på udden 1170). Reformation 1527 kronan. 1597 donation till Carl Carlsson Gyllenhielm; slott 1639–1648; 12 års polsk fångenskap dessförinnan; Gyllenhielmska skolan 1629 (Sveriges första folkskola, till 1987). Seved Bååt tre våningar; reduktion 1699. Brand julen 1774 under Adam Jakob von Schoting — magasin/fähus ~150 år. Eskilstuna 1939; restaurering 1952–53; idag hotell/restaurang/konferens (boende i övriga hus, inte i slottsbyggnaden). Mörk historia: fångenskap, brand, förfall — inte spökbevis. Cronstedt (efter 1779, dom/benådning) är historisk person; koppling till huva-gestalten är spekulation.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE & HOTELL: Officiell spöksida; Ekuriren. Fredlig vålnad ibland kopplad till Gyllenhielm. Medium 2008: »Här finns bara snälla spöken«. VITTNESMÅL: Maria i vinkällaren — lång mörk huva-gestalt efter vikingamiddag; fotsteg, dörrar, nycklar. Cronstedt-hypotes spekulativ. Herrgårdsgäster 2007 hörde ljud — hotellet noterar senare drop-in-gäster ovanför som naturlig förklaring. OMRÅDEN: källarvalv, korridorer, salonger, park. Håll isär från dokumenterad historia.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Sundbyholms Slott vid Mälaren norr om Eskilstuna är ett 1600-talsslott i vikingatida landskap med Sigurdsristningen och Sveriges första folkskola. Johannitiskt klostergods, Gyllenhielms byggherrskap 1639–1648, branden 1774 och Eskilstunas restaurering ger stark historisk tyngd. Hotellets spökberättelser om huva-gestalt i källaren och vänliga närvaror hålls isär från dokumenterad Gyllenhielm-historia. Boka officiellt; besök ristningen; respektera hotell och reservat.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt slotts hotell — boka endast via officiella kanaler. Boende i övriga byggnader, inte i själva slottet. Respektera gäster, personal och nattlig tystnad. Källare endast med tillträde. Sigurdsristningen och naturområden är öppna — skada inte ristningen; gå inte in i stängda byggnader.

places.name: Teleborgs Slott
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Teleborgs Slott rises like a fairy-tale Rhine Ritterburg on a rocky point in Lake Trummen, south of Växjö — one of Sweden's most photogenic Neo-Gothic castles, finished in 1900. Count Fredrik Bonde af Björnö commissioned Malmö architects Harald Boklund and August Lindvall to build it as a (slightly delayed) wedding gift / morgongåva for his much younger second wife Anna Koskull, for whom he had once been guardian; locals coined the wordplay "Vad gör inte en Bonde för sin Koskull." The site earlier held the Tuvan (Tufvan) estate, where poet-bishop Esaias Tegnér lived 1825–1827. Fredrik died in 1909 and Anna in 1917; childless, the house passed to nephew Christer Bonde (girls' boarding school, pension, 1931 park), then sold to Växjö in 1964. Since 2003 it has been a castle hotel, restaurant and conference venue; SVT filmed Stjärnorna på slottet here in 2017–2018. Folklore includes story walks, park spirits, and Countess Ulla Bonde's accounts of footsteps and doors she attributed to house-trolls Tulle and Tjita rather than ghosts; some popular tellings loosely link a female presence to Anna. Haunted Sweden keeps the documented Bonde romance and early deaths separate from those unverified reports. Book overnight; walk the public park and Trummen paths; respect hotel areas.
places.whyItFitsHauntedSweden: Iconic Småland fairy-tale castle hotel: Neo-Gothic towers on Trummen, wedding-gift origin, Tegnér layer, municipal park and Teleborg Nature Reserve, overnight stay and TV fame. Visual 10/10, historical 9.5/10, architectural 10/10, folklore 8.5/10, paranormal reputation 8.5/10, overnight potential 10/10 — Haunted Sweden Score 9.3. Premium content VERY HIGH; research confidence HIGH (history) / MEDIUM (paranormal). Verification mission: overnight, night photography, park walk, staff interviews, compare storyteller lore with Wikipedia/hotel/Växjö sources.
places.shortDescription: 1900 Neo-Gothic wedding-gift castle hotel on Lake Trummen — Bonde–Koskull romance, Tegnér's Tuvan, fairy-tale towers, and local ghost/troll storytelling rather than a single official named haunting.
places.history: DOCUMENTED: Teleborgs slott stands on a rocky lakeside site at Lake Trummen in Växjö municipality (Småland / Kronoberg), today beside Linnæus University and Teleborg slottspark, with Teleborgs naturreservat to the south. EARLIER ESTATE: The place succeeded the country estate Tuvan / Tufvan, built 1819 by Växjö tanner (Sven Johan) Björklund. Poet and later bishop Esaias Tegnér lived in the then main house 1825–1827 before moving to Växjö bishop's residence; a memorial stone raised 1900 by Fredrik Bonde and Anna Koskull commemorates Tegnér at "Tufvan now called Theleborg." Nearby village name Telestad underlies "Teleborg"; farms were consolidated under Tuvan in the 1840s. CASTLE: Count Gustav Fredrik Bonde af Björnö (1842–1909) bought the estate mid-1890s and in 1896 commissioned architects Harald Boklund and August Lindvall (Lindvall & Boklund, Malmö) for a romantic Neo-Gothic "knight's castle" inspired by Rhine / German late-medieval models — granite and brick cladding, three storeys, square main tower and smaller round tower. Construction generally dated 1896/97–1900; completed 1900 as a wedding gift (morgongåva), somewhat delayed, to his second wife Anna Koskull (1868–1917). Contemporary scandal: Bonde divorced first wife Charlotta Horatia Marryat (five children) and in 1889 married Anna, ~26 years younger, for whom he had been guardian — feeding the local catchphrase "Vad gör inte en Bonde för sin Koskull." Hotel history cites cost 192,772 kronor and 80 öre; materials from Torpa and Västervik area, tile stoves from Gothenburg, ironwork from Copenhagen. The couple did not live permanently there at first; after Fredrik's death in 1909 Anna moved in until her death in 1917 (electrification and bathroom 1915 per Slottsguiden). Childless; estate in fideikommiss passed to nephew Count Christer Bonde (1869–1956) — briefly castle pension and girls' boarding school, then from 1931 his residence and creation of the castle park. Son Fredrik Ulf Bonde inherited 1956; summer use under sister Ulla Bonde until sale. MODERN: Sold to Växjö city 1964 for 3.5 million SEK (fideikommiss wound up). Later municipal/company ownership (Vöfab / Videum cited in sources); hotel, restaurant and conference since 2003 (R&C Gastronomi among operators). SVT's Stjärnorna på slottet filmed at Teleborg summers 2017 and 2018 (Visit Växjö). Park: formal and nature sections with large trees; public paths around Trummen. DARK / EMOTIONAL HISTORY (documented only): Divorce and age-gap marriage scandal; Fredrik's death only ~9 years after completion; Anna's death eight years later at 49; childless line and sale out of the family — romantic tragedy of short shared happiness, not invented crimes or haunt-proof.
places.legend: FOLKLORE (not verified history): Teleborg lacks a single nationally fixed "White Lady" dossier comparable to older medieval castles, but local storytelling treats it as haunted. Guide/storyteller Vibeke Hyltén-Cavallius (local press) runs park and castle narrative walks claiming ghosts in the house and park — including a tradition of five dogs of former owners buried in the park — and says ghosts want the castle properly cared for; she also wrote a children's tale of two forest trolls who become castle ghosts. Countess Ulla Bonde, last family resident before the 1964 sale, told interviewers she did not believe in ghosts (despite Bonde family ghost lore at other seats) but believed in house-trolls Tulle and Tjita: evenings alone she and her watchdog heard footsteps and doors opening; they walked the house and found no one — she felt the trolls watched over her. ANNA KOSKULL: Because the castle is her wedding gift and she died relatively young in the house era, some informal / visitor tellings associate a female presence or upper-floor lights with Anna — present as speculative folklore, not archival fact. WITNESS-STYLE REPORTS (anecdotal / storyteller — not scientific investigations): footsteps in empty corridors; doors opening/closing; unexplained sounds; lights in upper rooms; cold spots and watched feeling in salons and on the main staircase — typical manor-hotel motifs repeated on walks and guest talk. SPECIAL AREAS: (1) Main staircase — architectural set-piece, often in stories. (2) Upper floors — lights and activity talk. (3) Historic salons — atmosphere. (4) Castle park — mist, dog graves lore, evening walks. (5) Lakeside / Trummen — photography and reflections. ATMOSPHERE: Fairy-tale towers and battlements, granite/brick façades, stone stairs, park oaks and beeches, evening light on Trummen. INVESTIGATION IDEAS: overnight; EVP in salons with permission; park after dark; Trummen night walk; history vs folklore; night photography. BEST CONDITIONS: autumn evenings, heavy fog, rain after sunset, winter darkness, overnight. Keep DOCUMENTED Bonde–Koskull / Tegnér history separate from FOLKLORE and anecdotal reports above.
places.safetyNote: Active castle hotel, restaurant and conference venue — book only via official Teleborgs Slott channels. Respect guests, staff, fire rules and night quiet. Interiors and private floors are not free exploration. Castle park and lakeside paths have public access — stay on marked routes, respect Teleborg Nature Reserve rules, and do not enter closed hotel or university buildings.
places.shortDescriptionSv: Nygotiskt sagoslott 1900 vid Trummen — Bondes bröllopsgåva till Anna Koskull, Tegnérs Tuvan, hotell idag och lokal spök-/trollberättartradition.
places.historySv: DOKUMENTERAT: Teleborgs slott, Växjö, vid sjön Trummen. Tidigare Tuvan/Tufvan (1819); Esaias Tegnér bodde där 1825–1827. Greve Fredrik Bonde af Björnö lät Lindvall & Boklund (Harald Boklund, August Lindvall) bygga nygotiskt riddarslott 1896/97–1900 som morgongåva till andra hustrun Anna Koskull (förmyndarskap/skandal; »Vad gör inte en Bonde för sin Koskull«). Fredrik dog 1909, Anna 1917; barnlöst. Brorsonen Christer Bonde — flickpension/pensionat, slottspark 1931. Sålt till Växjö stad 1964 (3,5 mkr). Hotell/restaurang/konferens sedan 2003; Stjärnorna på slottet 2017–2018. Teleborgs naturreservat söder om parken. Mörk/emotionell dokumenterad historia: kort lycka, tidiga dödsfall — inte spökbevis.
places.legendSv: FOLKLORE: Berättarvandringar (t.ex. Vibeke Hyltén-Cavallius) om spöken i slott och park (bl.a. begravda hundar). Grevinnan Ulla Bonde trodde inte på spöken men på trollen Tulle och Tjita — fotsteg och dörrar när hon var ensam. Anna Koskull kopplas ibland spekulativt till kvinnlig närvaro. Anekdoter: fotsteg, ljus, dörrar, köld. OMRÅDEN: huvudtrappa, övre våningar, salonger, park, sjösida. Håll isär från dokumenterad Bonde-historia.
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummarySv: Teleborgs Slott vid Trummen i Växjö är ett av Sveriges mest fotogena nygotiska sagoslott, färdigt 1900 som Fredrik Bondes bröllopsgåva till Anna Koskull. Tegnér bodde tidigare på Tuvan. Familjen Bonde sålde till Växjö 1964; idag hotell, restaurang och konferens (Stjärnorna på slottet 2017–18). Lokal folklore om spöken och Ulla Bondes troll hålls isär från dokumenterad bygg- och familjehistoria. Boka officiellt; respektera hotell och park.
places.safetyNoteSv: Aktivt slotts hotell — boka endast via officiella kanaler. Respektera gäster, personal och nattlig tystnad. Interiör är inte fri utforskning. Slottspark och sjöstigar är öppna — håll dig till markerade leder och naturreservatets regler.

places.name: Färna Herrgård
places.hauntedSwedenAppSummary: Färna Herrgård sits between lakes Norrsjön and Lillsjön in Bergslagen's historic Färna ironworks community (Skinnskatteberg) — more than four centuries of documented bruk history. Crown hammer works are attested from 1607; widow Edla Widiksdotter expanded the works in the 1630s; Wilckens and Jacob Ramsell built the first manor in 1776 and founded Sweden's largest fideikommiss by area (1789). Count Carl Johan von Hermansson remodelled the yellow-white timber manor to its present look in 1857; his son Carl Fredrik commissioned Lars Israel Wahlman's unique slag-stone mausoleum (1904–05, byggnadsminne 2015) overlooking Lillsjön — remains later moved to Gunnilbo churchyard. Iron forging ended around 1930; only foundations of the works remain. Since 1994 the Engström family has run hotel, spa and restaurant amid park, forest and Ekomuseum Bergslagen landscape. Local press records guest reports of a coachman spirit in the southern wing who closes doors and tucks guests in; mausoleum and ironworks ruins add atmosphere without inventing hauntings. Haunted Sweden keeps bruk chronology separate from folklore. Book overnight; respect hotel and private areas.
